ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: From a Kid to a Champion

fullPassage:
My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf. But there were a couple of more steep slopes ahead, and I doubted we had a chance. Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!"

For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.

Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line."

Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes.

He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved ①<u>feeling</u> the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race ②<u>was held</u> in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Excited by ③<u>what</u> he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was ④<u>waited</u> at the finish line.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ waited → waiting: Gabriel was waiting(진행형) = 기다리고 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ waited → waiting: 'was + V-ing' 과거진행형. was waited는 수동태가 되어 의미 불일치.
❌ ① feeling: love + 동명사 적절.
❌ ② was held: 수동태 적절.
❌ ③ what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 적절.
det.tip: be + V-ing = 진행형. be + p.p. = 수동태. 'was waiting'(기다리고 있었다) vs. 'was waited'(기다려졌다).

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, ①<u>where</u> only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had ②<u>rarely</u> cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in ③<u>riding</u> on hills and mountains, so he was always the first ④<u>arriving</u> at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① arriving → to arrive: the first + to-V 구문. 서수/최상급 뒤 to부정사.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ riding: 전치사 in + 동명사 적절.
❌ ① where: 선행사 team → 관계부사 where 적절.
❌ ② rarely: 부사 적절.
✅ ④ arriving → to arrive: 'the first to arrive'가 원문. the first/last + to-V.
det.tip: the first/last/only + to-V(to부정사). 전치사 + V-ing(동명사).

questions.passage: Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I ①<u>had not crashed</u>, Gabriel ②<u>would have come</u> in first place. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you ③<u>could</u> do it." It was the first time he had not ④<u>addressing</u> me as "kid."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ addressing → addressed: had not addressed = 과거완료. had + p.p. 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ addressing → addressed: 'had not addressed'가 원문. 과거완료(had + p.p.).
❌ ① had not crashed: 가정법 과거완료 if절 적절.
❌ ② would have come: 가정법 과거완료 주절 적절.
❌ ③ could: 시제 일치(knew → could) 적절.
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: If + had p.p., would have p.p. 과거완료: had + p.p.(과거분사).

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally ①<u>paid off</u> in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, I was riding in front of Gabriel to ②<u>shield</u> him from the headwind. Our team was far ③<u>ahead</u> of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to ④<u>surrender</u> on his behalf.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① surrender(항복하다) → continue(계속하다): 대신 계속 가라고 재촉한 것이지 항복하라는 것이 아님.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ ahead(앞서): 팀이 앞서 있었음.
❌ ① paid off(결실을 맺다): 노력의 결과 적절.
❌ ② shield(보호하다): 바람을 막아주는 맥락.
✅ ④ surrender → continue: 'urged me to continue on his behalf'가 원문.
det.tip: continue(계속하다) ↔ surrender(항복하다). 'on one's behalf' = ~을 대신하여.

questions.passage: As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the ①<u>glory</u> should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the ②<u>pride</u> in his eyes. He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not ③<u>addressed</u> me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears ④<u>dried</u> up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ dried(말랐다) → welled(솟구쳤다): 감동으로 눈물이 '솟구친' 것이지 '마른' 것이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ dried → welled: 'tears welled up'(눈물이 고였다)가 원문. 감동의 눈물.
❌ ① glory(영광): 영광이 Gabriel에게 가야 한다는 맥락.
❌ ② pride(자부심): 눈에서 자부심을 볼 수 있었음.
❌ ③ addressed(칭하다): 처음으로 'kid'라고 부르지 않음.
det.tip: well up(솟구치다) ↔ dry up(마르다). 'tears welled up' = 눈물이 고이다.

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always __________ in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산악 경주에서 항상 뒤처졌다(fell behind).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ fell behind: 평지는 잘했지만 산악에서 뒤처짐. 네덜란드가 평탄하여 경사 경험 부족.
❌ ① got ahead(앞서다): 반대 의미.
❌ ② kept up(따라갔다): 뒤처졌다는 문맥과 불일치.
❌ ④ broke free(벗어나다): 경주 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: fall behind = 뒤처지다. get ahead = 앞서다. keep up = 보조 맞추다.

questions.passage: He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line." Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경쟁자를 근소한 차이로(by a nose) 앞서 결승선 통과.
det.analysis:
✅ ① by a nose: 'right on my tail' = 바로 뒤를 쫓음 → 아슬아슬한 차이.
❌ ② by a landslide(압도적으로): 바로 뒤를 쫓았으므로 모순.
❌ ③ with ease(쉽게): 라이벌이 바로 뒤를 쫓음.
❌ ④ without effort(노력 없이): 전력 질주한 맥락.
det.tip: by a nose = 아슬아슬하게. by a landslide = 압도적으로.

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps!"
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Bliksem은 열두 살에 첫 자전거 대회에 참가했다.
Gabriel은 경주 전에 Bliksem에게 사인을 해주었다.
Bliksem은 다른 선수들보다 두 바퀴 앞서 우승했다.
Bliksem은 네덜란드에서 자전거보다 사람이 더 많은 나라에서 태어났다.

det.korean: 두 바퀴 앞서(outran by two laps) 우승.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 두 바퀴 앞서 우승: 'outran the others by two laps' 원문 일치.
❌ ① 자전거보다 사람이 많다: 반대(more bicycles than people).
❌ ③ 열두 살: eleven(열한 살).
❌ ④ 경주 전 사인: 우승 후에 사인.
det.tip: outrun = ~보다 앞서 달리다. by two laps = 두 바퀴 차이로.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation. The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Gabriel은 주저 없이 자신의 자전거를 Bliksem에게 주었다.
경주가 끝날 때까지 Gabriel은 따라잡지 못했다.

det.korean: Gabriel이 주저 없이(without hesitation) 자전거를 내줌.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 주저 없이 자전거 제공: 'offered me his bike without hesitation' 원문 일치.
❌ ① 100 km: 250 km가 원문.
❌ ② 산악 구간: cobblestone(자갈) 구간에서 펑크.
❌ ④ 따라잡지 못함: 10 km 남았을 때 따라잡음.
det.tip: cobblestone = 자갈/조약돌. flat tire = 타이어 펑크.

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Bliksem은 Gabriel 앞에서 달리며 맞바람을 막아주었다.
Bliksem은 도로의 구멍 때문에 넘어졌고, Gabriel은 다치지 않았다.

det.korean: ② Gabriel은 다치지 않았다 → 더 심하게 다쳤다: 'Gabriel's injury was more serious'가 원문.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 불일치: Gabriel의 부상이 더 심각했음.
❌ ① 일치: 'riding in front of Gabriel to shield him'.
❌ ③ 일치: 'All four of us fell'.
❌ ④ 일치: 'the other teams passed us by'.
det.tip: slightly wounded = 가벼운 부상. more serious = 더 심각한.

questions.passage: For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain."
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Gabriel(멘토)이 Bliksem(제자)을 이끌고, Bliksem이 성장하여 팀 리더가 되는 신뢰와 성장의 이야기.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 멘토와 제자: Gabriel의 지도 → Bliksem의 성장 → 리더십 승계.
❌ ① 개인 기술만: 팀워크와 멘토링이 핵심.
❌ ② 은퇴 준비: 은퇴 자체가 아닌 관계에 초점.
❌ ③ 규칙과 전략: 전략이 아닌 인간관계.
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 메시지. 멘토-제자 관계 + 성장.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation. When there were only 10 km left, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line." Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose. The crowd roared tremendously.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: How to Win a Race Alone

det.korean: 팀워크와 희생을 통한 승리: Gabriel의 자전거 양보 + 팀원 지원 → Bliksem 우승.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Victory Through Teamwork and Sacrifice: Gabriel의 희생(자전거 양보) + 팀 지원 → 승리.
❌ ① Alone: 혼자가 아닌 팀으로 이김.
❌ ③ Dangers: 위험이 아닌 극복에 초점.
❌ ④ Individual Talent: 개인 기술보다 팀워크 강조.
det.tip: 제목 = 글의 핵심을 한 문장으로. sacrifice = 희생.

questions.passage: Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid." Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"
questions.stem: 위 글에서 Gabriel이 반복적으로 말하는 "Never stop pedaling"이 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 어떤 어려움이 있어도 포기하지 말라는 격려

det.korean: "Never stop pedaling" = 어떤 어려움이 있어도 포기하지 말라는 인생의 격려.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 포기하지 말라: 오르막이 고통스럽지만 정상의 풍경은 환상적 → 인내의 메시지.
❌ ① 기술적 조언: 단순 기술이 아닌 삶의 교훈.
❌ ② 안전 수칙: 안전이 아닌 동기부여.
❌ ④ 앞서 나가라: 앞서기보다 멈추지 말라는 격려.
det.tip: 함축의미 = 표면적 의미 너머의 깊은 뜻. pedaling = 페달 밟기 → 비유: 계속 노력하기.

questions.passage: As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes. <u>He</u> said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 He가 가리키는 대상은?

det.korean: Gabriel: Bliksem이 포디움에서 Gabriel을 바라봤고, Gabriel이 "Captain"이라고 부름.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Gabriel: 앞 문장에서 Gabriel을 바라봄 → 그의 눈에서 자부심 → he = Gabriel.
❌ ② Bliksem: 화자 자신(I)이므로 he가 될 수 없음.
❌ ③ 팀원: 팀원들은 뒤에 등장(teammates approached).
❌ ④ 경쟁 팀: 문맥에 없음.
det.tip: 지칭추론: 대명사 앞뒤 문맥을 확인. 'looked over → see the pride in his eyes → He said'.

questions.passage: When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" <u>He</u> smiled and said, "If you win, you can."
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 He가 가리키는 대상은?

det.korean: Gabriel Martinez: Bliksem이 Gabriel에게 사인을 요청 → Gabriel이 미소 지으며 대답.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Gabriel Martinez: 직전 대화에서 Gabriel에게 말을 걸었으므로 He = Gabriel.
❌ ① Bliksem: 화자(I)이므로 He가 아님.
❌ ③ 다른 선수: 대화 상대가 Gabriel.
❌ ④ 관중: 문맥에 없음.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without __________, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Paris-Roubaix 경주에서 자갈길 때문에 타이어가 펑크 나자, Gabriel은 __________ 없이 자신의 자전거를 내주었다."

det.korean: 주저함(hesitation) 없이 자전거를 내줌.
det.analysis: 원문: 'Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation.' → '없이'에 해당하는 단어 = hesitation.
det.tip: without hesitation = 주저 없이. hesitate(동사) → hesitation(명사).

questions.passage: I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. __________ (motivate) by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: Gabriel의 격려에 동기 부여되어(Motivated) 훈련에 참여.
det.analysis: 주어(I)가 동기를 '받는' 입장 → 과거분사(Motivated). 분사구문: Motivated by ~ = ~에 의해 동기 부여되어.
det.tip: 분사구문: 주어가 능동 → V-ing, 수동 → p.p. motivate(동기 부여하다) → Motivated(동기 부여된).

questions.passage: The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, __________. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes.

[ I / felt / like / the / glory / should / go / to / Gabriel ]

det.analysis: feel like + S + V = ~인 것 같다. 'the glory should go to Gabriel' = 영광이 Gabriel에게 가야 한다.
det.tip: feel like + 절 = ~인 것 같다/~하고 싶다. should = ~해야 한다.
